title: link-training-glitch-repro-attempt-field-journal
summary: Field journal capturing on-call observations and repro attempts for an intermittent NVLink link-training failure that cascaded into driver reinitialization and a kernel oops across a small subset of nodes. Includes timeline, commands, raw excerpts, hypotheses, and a proposed emergency runbook draft.
body:
Context:
This is a running, informal log capturing the week of 2029-03-15 to 2029-03-18 when several GPU nodes in rack-r12 showed transient NVLink retrain events. Two nodes (r12-n08, r12-n12) progressed from correctable ECC spikes to a full driver reinit and a single kernel oops (no core dump produced). Events are intermittent — ~1-2x/day per node — and seem to cluster around brief PDU micro-sags during scheduled rack maintenance on 2029-03-16 (ops note).

Top-level hypothesis (current):
- Primary: brief voltage transients (PDU switching) cause PHY-level retrain on NVLink fabric; retrain can fail or cause lane negotiation flaps which the driver handles by reinitialization. On unlucky timing the reinit hits a kernel-path that walks dependent pointers and triggers an oops.
- Secondary: one NVLink retimer/retimer-firmware revision in nodes r12-n08 and r12-n12 is more sensitive; both share same board rev and vendor retimer fw v2.3.
- Compounding: ECC correctable error (CE) rate increases during link noise; correctable errors saturate GPU ECC counters and trigger SRE/alert thresholds which lead to page retire/eviction heuristics and increased scheduler churn.

Observed signals (raw):
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC snapshots during incident (excerpt):
  * r12-n08, 2029-03-16T14:12:10Z: correctable_errors: 0 -> 12 in 7s; uncorrectable_errors: 0
  * r12-n12, 2029-03-16T14:12:12Z: correctable_errors spike 0 -> 9 in 5s
- dmesg / journalctl kernel oops snippet (r12-n08, 2029-03-16T14:12:13Z):
  "[  12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00:00: decoupled from link training, nvlink-phy-timeout=1500ms
   [  12345.679250] nvidia: kernel module reinit requested
   [  12345.680000] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000008
   [  12345.680100] RIP: 0010:0xdeadbeefbeef0001
   [  12345.680200] Call Trace: <nvidia_reinit_work+0x1f5/0x270>
  "
- PSU/rack PDUs: ops pdu-log shows a 150ms ~1.8-2.5V droop on +12V rail to rack-r12 PDU outlet group during fuse testing at 2029-03-16T14:12Z. Correlation window aligns to NVLink events above.
- Telemetry: host-side PCIe logs show link retrain flags and FLR count +1 at same timestamp (small).

Repro attempts performed so far (field lab + oncall):
1) Controlled retimer stress: in test-lab we injected a 300-500us voltage dip on a board with retimer fw v2.3 -> reproduced NVLink lane retrain, but no kernel oops (driver gracefully retrained in lab).
2) Repeat with slightly longer dip (~1.8ms) -> observed driver reinit in lab once, but oops only reproduced when simultaneous high ECC CE background load present (running memtest-like kernel loads).
3) Swap GPU board between r12-n08 and r12-n05 (different board rev) -> r12-n05 with board rev of n05 did not exhibit oops under same injected dip. Suggests hardware rev sensitivity.
4) Boot with "nvidia.NVreg_RestrictVBlank=1" and with PCIe ASPM disabled -> little effect on retrain events.

What we collected (artifacts):
- full journalctl -k logs for r12-n08 and r12-n12 (attached to SRE-4123)
- nvidia-smi wrappers (snapshots every 2s for 2 hours) in /var/tmp/sre/nvlink-2029-03-16
- PDU logs from ops pinned in Confluence link in the ticket

Open questions (notes to self):
- Are firmware revisions for the retimers identical for both suspect nodes? We saw fw v2.3, but need full micro-builds (ops to confirm).
- Can we selectively throttle ECC background workload in prod to see if oops frequency drops (non-intrusive experiment)?
- Does the kernel path that oops have a known race or earlier bug report? Search kernel mailing lists and NVIDIA driver bug db for "reinit NULL deref".

Quick mitigation steps (executed):
- 2029-03-16 14:25Z: cordoned r12-n08 + r12-n12, drained running jobs to reduce blast radius.
- 14:28Z: downgraded power maintenance schedule and requested ops to avoid PDU fuse test on that PDU bank until nodes are moved to spare racking.
- 14:40Z: added temporary alert exception for CE bursts for the two nodes to avoid noisy pager churn while we investigate (SRE lead approved).

Proposed emergency runbook (draft - needs review):
- Trigger: any node that reports (a) NVLink retrain flag + (b) CE spike > 10 within 60s.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Cordon node, set job-run-scaler to 0 for that node.
  2) Capture memory of GPU: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC; nvml top output; copy dmesg & full journal; tar /var/log/nvidia* and /var/log/kern*; run lspci -vvv > /tmp/lspci-$(hostname).txt
  3) Check PDU logs for events in +/- 120s window with ops.
  4) If retrain persists after 3 reboots -> move node to quarantine rack, swap board to spare, and repro in lab.
- Long term: replace retimer boards on nodes matching board-rev X and retimer-fw v2.3; schedule batch replacement and firmware update to v2.4 once vendor confirms fixes.

Repro playbook (lab):
- Pre-reqs: test bench with ability to pulse +12V rail (controlled), spare board with identical rev, and memtest stress harness to produce ECC CE background.
- 1) Boot node with stress harness (ECC pressure) and monitor nvidia-smi errors with script at 1s sampling.
- 2) Pulse +12V for 1.5ms at 1.9-2.2V dip; repeat 10x; observe retrain counts and driver reinit.
- 3) If driver reinit occurs: enable kgdb and attempt kdump capturing (capture early panics); if oops, collect module addresses for NVIDIA driver and file for vendor.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Marisol: confirm retimer firmware micro-builds and send to vendor for quick review (due 2029-03-21).
- Liu: schedule spare board swap for r12-n08 and repro in lab (due 2029-03-22).
- Evan: draft a kernel/driver issue with stack trace and attach to SRE-4123 for vendor escalation (due 2029-03-20).
- Aisha: update alerts to suppress CE-burst noise for quarantined nodes (completed).

Notes & heuristics learned (informal):
- Not every retrain causes an oops; there is a confluence of small voltage sag + background ECC pressure + older retimer fw that together push the driver into a failing path.
- In several successful lab repros the driver reinit completed cleanly; kernel oops was a lower probability event but consistently reproducible with precise timing.
- Quick wins: move maintenance PDUs away from racks with sensitive rev hardware and throttle maintenance fuse tests; both reduced incidence in the field.

Unresolved items for review meeting:
- Do we accept a band-aid (alert suppression + node quarantine + PDU ops change) vs immediate hardware replacement? Cost/ops tradeoffs needed.
- Should we build a small telemetry probe to detect NVLink PHY retrain flags and proactively migrate jobs before CE spikes? (Possible, but needs infra work).

Appendix - Useful commands (collected):
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTILIZATION,MEMORY
- watch -n1 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv"  # internal wrapper used in snapshots
- sudo journalctl -k --since "2029-03-16 14:10" --until "2029-03-16 14:20" > /tmp/klog-14-10-14-20.log
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0000:3b:00.0/information
- git issue: GH-678 infra/retimer-firmware-update (WIP)

End of field journal. This is intentionally rough — please comment inline, add repro observations, and tag vendor escalation if you have low-level firmware/driver insight.

Quick link: SRE-4123 (primary incident ticket)
